description: Canonical metric formulas in the GASP formula grammar (grammar reference: gasp-wiki-mcp/src/formula.ts). Keyed by formula id: the graph node id when the metric has one, else the metric slug with underscores, prefixed by department when two metrics share a slug. Ratios are unscaled and `unit` says how to display them; subtracting two dates gives elapsed days. `field.` refs resolve to ontology.json fields (each belongs to one or more datasets), `metric.` refs to other formula ids. Filter literals on enum fields must be declared values. Entries without a single formula carry `notComputable` instead.

mrr.notes: Annual contracts contribute annual value / 12. Excludes one-time fees, trials and non-guaranteed usage. by_plan returns one row per plan the subscriptions are priced by. by_segment returns one row per customer segment, read from the subscription snapshot at period end.

forms.O: (metric.mrr - window(sum(field.mrr_change where field.expansion_classification in ('pricing_adjustment', 'recontracting')), 12 month)) * 12 over cohort(field.customer_id, period_end)

arr.notes: ARR-M equals this formula. ARR-O subtracts the MRR change tagged pricing_adjustment or recontracting in the trailing 12 months for customers active at period end, so ARR-M minus ARR-O is the Durability Gap (core.md), a growth decomposition measured over the trailing year. by_segment returns one row per customer segment through MRR.

arpa.formula: metric.mrr / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_end
arpa.notes: by_segment returns one row per customer segment, since a blended ARPA across SMB and enterprise describes neither.

new_mrr.notes: by_segment returns one row per customer segment, which shows where new business lands.

expansion_mrr.notes: by_segment returns one row per customer segment, which shows where expansion comes from.

churned_mrr.notes: Churn events carry a negative mrr_change; the metric reports a positive amount. by_segment returns one row per customer segment, so churn concentrated in one segment is visible.

contraction_mrr.notes: Contraction events carry a negative mrr_change; the metric reports a positive amount. by_segment returns one row per customer segment, so downgrades concentrated in one segment are visible.

bundle_pricing_and_mrr_allocation.notComputable: An allocation method applied when recording item-level MRR (Item SSP / sum of SSPs x bundle price), not a reported metric.

nrr.formula: (metric.mrr at period_start + metric.expansion_mrr - metric.contraction_mrr - metric.churned_mrr) / metric.mrr at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

forms.O: (metric.mrr at period_start + sum(field.mrr_change where field.event_type = 'expansion' and field.expansion_classification in ('same_product', 'usage_realisation')) - metric.contraction_mrr - metric.churned_mrr) / metric.mrr at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)
forms.M: (metric.mrr at period_start + sum(field.mrr_change where field.event_type in ('expansion', 'reactivation') and field.expansion_classification in ('same_product', 'new_module', 'new_buying_centre', 'pricing_adjustment', 'recontracting', 'usage_realisation')) - metric.contraction_mrr - metric.churned_mrr) / metric.mrr at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

variants.adjusted: (sum(field.mrr_start) + sum(field.mrr_change where field.event_type in ('expansion', 'contraction', 'churn') and field.change_nature = 'permanent')) / sum(field.mrr_start) over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

nrr.notes: Period is trailing 12 months, over the customers active at period start (cohort method, the investor-comparable basis). NRR-O counts expansion tagged same_product or usage_realisation. NRR-M counts every expansion classification plus reactivation of cohort customers; customers who churned before the period and return are new business. The main formula is core.md's formula method. by_segment returns one row per customer segment, because retention differs most between SMB and enterprise; each snapshot and event counts in the segment it carries.

grr.formula: (metric.mrr at period_start - metric.contraction_mrr - metric.churned_mrr) / metric.mrr at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

variants.per_customer: sum(min(field.mrr_end, field.mrr_start)) / sum(field.mrr_start) over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)
variants.adjusted: (sum(field.mrr_start) + sum(field.mrr_change where field.event_type in ('contraction', 'churn') and field.change_nature = 'permanent')) / sum(field.mrr_start) over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

grr.notes: Period is trailing 12 months. The main formula is core.md's formula method, the canonical one; variants.per_customer is the cohort method, which nets each customer's movements within the period and so reads equal to or higher than the main formula. Capped at 100% by construction. by_segment returns one row per customer segment, because retention differs most between SMB and enterprise; each snapshot and event counts in the segment it carries.

logo_churn_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'churn') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_start
logo_churn_rate.notes: by_segment returns one row per customer segment, since SMB logos usually churn at several times the enterprise rate.

revenue_churn_rate.notes: by_segment returns one row per customer segment, so churn concentrated in one segment is visible.

nps.formula: (count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'customer' and field.nps_score >= 9) - count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'customer' and field.nps_score <= 6)) / count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'customer') * 100
nps.notes: Reported as a score from -100 to 100, so the x 100 is part of the definition.

cac.formula: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'new')

forms.O: (sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm') + sum(field.cost where field.cost_function in ('implementation', 'onboarding'))) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'new')
forms.M: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'new')

cac.notes: GTM cost is ATL cost_function gtm (sales and marketing). CAC-O adds implementation and onboarding cost per the ATL bridge. by_cost_centre slices GTM cost by cost centre; the denominator stays the whole population of new customers, so the rows sum to CAC.

ltv.notes: LTV-M equals this formula. LTV-O uses contribution margin (gross_margin.forms.O) in place of gross margin.

forms.O: (sum(field.revenue) - sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'infrastructure') - sum(field.cost where field.cost_function in ('support', 'success_engineering', 'implementation', 'onboarding'))) / sum(field.revenue)

gross_margin.notes: COGS is cost_function infrastructure (hosting, compute, payment processing). Canonical Gross Margin equals GM-M; GM-O (contribution margin) also subtracts support, success engineering, implementation and onboarding cost. Revenue is GAAP recognised revenue.

total_active_partners.notes: Active means activity in the trailing 12 months: deals registered, deals closed, certification maintained or engagement threshold met. Encoded through the partner status flag.

partner_tier_distribution.notes: Reported per tier: partners in the tier over all partners, on the period-end partner snapshot.

partner_activation_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.partner_id where in_period(field.partner_recruited_date) and field.partner_status = 'active') at period_end / count_distinct(field.partner_id where in_period(field.partner_recruited_date)) at period_end
partner_activation_rate.notes: Partners recruited in the period who are active at period end over partners recruited in the period, as partnerships.md defines it. A partner moves from recruited to active status once productive (first deal registered or closed, or the engagement threshold met).

partner_churn_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.partner_id where in_period(field.partner_churn_date)) / count_distinct(field.partner_id where field.partner_status = 'active') at period_start
partner_churn_rate.notes: Partners with a churn date in the period over partners active at period start. by_partner_tier returns one row per partner tier, which tests whether tier benefits retain partners.

partner_sourced_revenue.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.partner_sourced = true and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

partner_influenced_revenue.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.partner_id is not null and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

channel_revenue_percentage.notes: Total revenue is GAAP recognised revenue.

average_partner_revenue.notes: Total partner revenue is partner_influenced_revenue: closed-won revenue on every deal with a partner attached, partner-sourced deals included.

deal_registration_to_close_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.registration_id where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count_distinct(field.registration_id where in_period(field.registration_date))
deal_registration_to_close_rate.notes: Registrations closed won in the period over registrations submitted in the period.

partner_win_rate.formula: count(field.opportunity_id where field.partner_id is not null and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count(field.opportunity_id where field.partner_id is not null and field.opportunity_stage in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost') and in_period(field.close_date))

partner_deal_size.formula: metric.partner_sourced_revenue / count(field.opportunity_id where field.partner_sourced = true and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

partner_sales_cycle.formula: median(field.close_date - field.registration_date where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))
partner_sales_cycle.notes: Registered deals only; measured from registration to close on the deal registration record.

partner_portal_engagement.notComputable: A family of portal activity measures (logins, downloads, modules accessed, registrations) with no single formula.

training_completion.notes: Denominator is partners enrolled in required training.

partner_nps.formula: (count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'partner' and field.nps_score >= 9) - count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'partner' and field.nps_score <= 6)) / count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'partner') * 100
partner_nps.notes: Same as NPS, computed on partner satisfaction surveys.

cost_of_partner_acquisition.formula: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'partner_program') / count_distinct(field.partner_id where in_period(field.partner_recruited_date))

partner_lifetime_value.notes: Average annual partner revenue assumes a 12-month period.

partner_roi.formula: (metric.partner_sourced_revenue - sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'partner_program')) / sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'partner_program')

resellers.notComputable: A partner-type grouping that applies existing metrics per type (key metric revenue per reseller), not a single formula.

referral_partners.notComputable: A partner-type grouping that applies existing metrics per type (key metric referrals per partner), not a single formula.

technology_partners_integrations.notComputable: A partner-type grouping that applies existing metrics per type (key metric customers using integration), not a single formula.

system_integrators_sis.notComputable: A partner-type grouping that applies existing metrics per type (key metric implementations delivered), not a single formula.

managed_service_providers_msps.notComputable: A partner-type grouping that applies existing metrics per type (key metric seats under management), not a single formula.

marketplace_revenue.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.channel = 'referral' and field.partner_sourced = true and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))
marketplace_revenue.notes: Marketplace deals are partner-sourced opportunities attributed to the marketplace listing. Tag them with channel referral and partner_sourced until a marketplace channel value is added.

marketplace_listings_performance.notComputable: A set of listing measures (views, trial starts, conversions, ratings) with no single formula.

pipeline_value.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount * field.stage_probability where field.opportunity_stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost'))
pipeline_value.notes: Weighted form is the main formula. Always state weighted or unweighted.

pipeline_coverage.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.opportunity_stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost')) / sum(field.quota)
pipeline_coverage.notes: Unweighted open pipeline (the unweighted variant of pipeline_value) over quota. The 3x to 4x benchmarks assume unweighted pipeline, since 1 / win rate already applies the conversion.

pipeline_velocity.formula: count(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost')) * metric.win_rate * metric.average_deal_size / metric.sales_cycle
pipeline_velocity.notes: Revenue per day. Markdown describes deal size as ACV in the levers list and average deal value in the formula.

win_rate.formula: count(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost') and in_period(field.close_date))
win_rate.notes: Excludes open deals and deals disqualified before the qualified stage. by_channel returns one row per acquisition channel the opportunities came through, the comparison behind channel budget decisions.

opportunity_to_close_rate.notes: Markdown states this is Win Rate measured from the opportunity stage.

acv.notes: ACV is recorded on the contract event (CEL). One-time fees are excluded by definition.

average_deal_size.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))
average_deal_size.notes: Uses total contract value, not annualised.

sales_cycle.formula: avg(field.close_date - field.opportunity_created_date where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

variants.median: median(field.close_date - field.opportunity_created_date where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

sales_cycle.notes: Mean days from opportunity creation to close for deals won in the period, as sales.md defines it. Report the median variant beside it to show outlier skew.

quota_attainment.notes: Individual form groups by rep_id; team form uses totals.

revenue_per_rep.notes: Total new revenue per quota-carrying rep.

ramp_time.notes: Per rep, from start date to consistently achieving quota. Convert days to months.

activity_metrics_diagnostic.notComputable: A diagnostic family of activity counts (calls, emails, meetings, demos) with no single formula.

services_attach_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.includes_services = true and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

average_services_deal_size.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.revenue_type = 'services') / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.revenue_type = 'services')
average_services_deal_size.notes: Services bookings divided by services engagements, one engagement per booked deal.

services_backlog.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.revenue_type = 'services' and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won') to_date - metric.services_revenue to_date
services_backlog.notes: Cumulative services booked minus cumulative services revenue recognised, to the end of the period.

services_gross_margin.notes: Direct delivery cost covers consultant salaries, travel and contractor costs.

project_margin.formula: (sum(field.project_revenue where in_period(field.project_completion_date)) - sum(field.project_cost where in_period(field.project_completion_date))) / sum(field.project_revenue where in_period(field.project_completion_date))
project_margin.notes: Margin on projects completed in the period.

realization_rate.notes: Hours worked at standard rate is taken from billable hours.

billable_utilization.notes: Available hours are total work hours minus PTO, holidays and company meetings.

total_utilization.notes: Non-billable productive time is training, pre-sales and internal projects.

bench_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.consultant_id where field.project_id is null) / count_distinct(field.consultant_id)
bench_rate.notes: Rows are consultant assignment records; a consultant with no project assignment is on the bench.

capacity.notes: Sum over consultants of available hours.

capacity_utilization.notes: Hours booked is taken as budgeted hours on sold projects.

on_time_delivery.formula: count_distinct(field.project_id where in_period(field.project_completion_date) and field.project_completion_date <= field.target_date) / count_distinct(field.project_id where in_period(field.project_completion_date))

on_budget_delivery.formula: count_distinct(field.project_id where in_period(field.project_completion_date) and field.hours_actual <= field.hours_budgeted) / count_distinct(field.project_id where in_period(field.project_completion_date))

project_duration_accuracy.notes: Per-project estimated duration over actual duration, averaged over projects completed in the period, so each project weighs the same. Target is 90 to 110 percent.

project_csat.formula: count(field.satisfaction_score where field.survey_type = 'project' and field.satisfaction_score >= 4) / count(field.satisfaction_score where field.survey_type = 'project')
project_csat.notes: Positive is the top two ratings on a 5-point scale. Surveyed at project completion.

project_nps.formula: (count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'project' and field.nps_score >= 9) - count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'project' and field.nps_score <= 6)) / count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'project') * 100
project_nps.notes: Reported as a score from -100 to 100, so the x 100 is part of the definition.

reference_ability.formula: count_distinct(field.project_id where in_period(field.project_completion_date) and field.referenceable = true) / count_distinct(field.project_id where in_period(field.project_completion_date))

revenue_per_consultant.notes: Benchmarks are annual, so use an annual period.

projects_per_consultant.formula: count_distinct(field.project_id where in_period(field.project_completion_date)) / count_distinct(field.consultant_id where in_period(field.project_completion_date))

services_pipeline.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.revenue_type = 'services' and field.opportunity_stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost')) at period_end

services_win_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.revenue_type = 'services' and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.revenue_type = 'services' and field.opportunity_stage in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost') and in_period(field.close_date))

time_to_start.notes: close_date on the project is the close date of the won opportunity.

ticket_volume.notes: Tickets created in period. by_ticket_type returns the count of each type for staffing; Ticket Distribution by Type (ticket_distribution_by_type) is the share.

tickets_per_customer.formula: metric.ticket_volume / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_end

ticket_backlog.formula: count_distinct(field.ticket_id where field.ticket_status in ('open', 'pending')) at period_end

ticket_distribution_by_type.notes: Reported per ticket type: tickets of the type created in the period over Ticket Volume (all tickets created in the period). The numerator counts tickets as Ticket Volume does.

frt.notes: Median, not average, to resist outlier skew.

resolution_time_time_to_resolution.notes: Computed over resolved tickets. by_ticket_type returns one row per ticket type, since a bug waits on engineering and a how-to question does not.

reopen_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.ticket_id where field.reopened = true) / count_distinct(field.ticket_id where field.ticket_status = 'resolved')
reopen_rate.notes: Resolved tickets include those since reopened.

csat.formula: count(field.satisfaction_score where field.survey_type = 'customer' and field.satisfaction_score >= 4) / count(field.satisfaction_score where field.survey_type = 'customer')
csat.notes: Positive is the top two ratings on a 5-point scale.

tickets_per_agent.notes: Agents are employees in the support department.

cost_per_ticket.formula: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'support') / count_distinct(field.ticket_id where field.ticket_status = 'resolved')

variants.customer_counts: (count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_end - count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'new')) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_start

logo_retention_rate.notes: by_segment returns one row per customer segment through Logo Churn Rate.

health_score.notes: The portfolio average of the composite score (0 to 100) across customers active at period end. The composite is built upstream from usage, engagement, support and commercial signals with weights calibrated to the company's own churn data; customer-success.md gives a reference weighting as a starting point. by_segment returns one row per customer segment, since a healthy average can hide a weak enterprise segment.

health_score_coverage.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.composite_score is not null) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active')
health_score_coverage.notes: Denominator is active accounts. Restrict to managed accounts or a revenue threshold by filtering the population. by_segment returns one row per customer segment, since coverage is usually required for enterprise accounts first.

at_risk_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.composite_score < 40) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.composite_score is not null)

variants.entered_at_risk: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.state_category = 'at_risk') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_start

at_risk_rate.notes: Health scores run 0 to 100; below 40 is at risk. Variant entered_at_risk is the flow: the share of customers active at period start who moved into the at_risk lifecycle state during the period (cel.md Lifecycle_State_Change). by_segment returns one row per customer segment, so risk in the segment that carries the most revenue is visible on its own.

qbr_completion.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.qbr_completed = true) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.qbr_due = true)
qbr_completion.notes: Counted per account: customers with a QBR held in the period (qbr_completed) over customers with a QBR due (qbr_due), both on the customer snapshot. customer-success.md defines it over eligible accounts.

executive_sponsor_coverage.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.contact_role = 'executive_sponsor' and field.contact_engaged = true) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active')
executive_sponsor_coverage.notes: Numerator counts accounts with at least one engaged contact whose role is executive_sponsor on the contact snapshot at period end. Denominator is active accounts; restrict to managed accounts by filtering the population.

contact_coverage.formula: count_distinct(field.contact_id where field.contact_engaged = true) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active')
contact_coverage.notes: Engaged contacts on the contact snapshot at period end over active accounts on the customer snapshot. An account with no contacts counts in the denominator.

expansion_rate.notes: by_segment returns one row per customer segment, since expansion headroom differs by segment.

license_utilization.formula: sum(field.seats_assigned where field.license_status = 'active') / sum(field.seats_purchased where field.license_status = 'active')
license_utilization.notes: Active licenses on the license snapshot at period end. Seats purchased is the entitlement the subscription grants; seats assigned is the number held by a named user. by_product returns one row per product the licenses cover.

upsell_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.amendment_type = 'upgrade') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.upgrade_eligible = true) at period_start

cross_sell_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.amendment_type = 'cross_sell') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_start

renewal_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.subscription_id where field.renewed = true and in_period(field.contract_end)) / count_distinct(field.subscription_id where in_period(field.contract_end))

variants.by_value: sum(field.renewal_amount where field.renewed = true and in_period(field.contract_end)) / sum(field.renewal_amount where in_period(field.contract_end))

renewal_rate.notes: Denominator is subscriptions whose term ended in the period.

renewal_forecast_accuracy.formula: 1 - abs(sum(field.forecast_renewal_amount where in_period(field.contract_end)) - sum(field.renewal_amount where in_period(field.contract_end) and field.renewed = true)) / sum(field.renewal_amount where in_period(field.contract_end) and field.renewed = true)

days_to_renewal.notes: Averaged over upcoming renewals at the snapshot date.

pipeline_hygiene_score.formula: (count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.required_fields_complete = true) / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id) + count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.updated_within_sla = true) / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id) + count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.close_date_valid = true) / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id) + count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.stage_accurate = true) / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id)) / 4

commit_accuracy.formula: count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.forecast_category = 'commit' and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.forecast_category = 'commit')

stage_conversion_rates.notes: Evaluate per stage by filtering field.stage to the stage of interest.

quote_to_order_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.order_id where in_period(field.order_completed_at)) / count_distinct(field.quote_id where in_period(field.quote_sent_at))
quote_to_order_rate.notes: Orders are those created from a quote in the period.

quote_accuracy.formula: count_distinct(field.quote_id where in_period(field.quote_sent_at) and field.revision_count = 0) / count_distinct(field.quote_id where in_period(field.quote_sent_at))

discount_rate.formula: (sum(field.list_price where in_period(field.quote_sent_at)) - sum(field.quoted_price where in_period(field.quote_sent_at))) / sum(field.list_price where in_period(field.quote_sent_at))

order_error_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.order_id where in_period(field.order_completed_at) and field.has_error = true) / count_distinct(field.order_id where in_period(field.order_completed_at))

billing_accuracy.formula: count_distinct(field.invoice_id where in_period(field.invoice_date) and field.invoice_corrected = false) / count_distinct(field.invoice_id where in_period(field.invoice_date))

invoice_cycle_time.notes: Calendar days, as revops.md states. A business-day count differs when the interval spans weekends or holidays.

billing_disputes.formula: count_distinct(field.invoice_id where in_period(field.invoice_date) and field.invoice_disputed = true) / count_distinct(field.invoice_id where in_period(field.invoice_date))
billing_disputes.notes: by_payment_status returns one row per payment status as of period end, since a dispute rate concentrated in unpaid invoices points at collections.

credit_memo_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.invoice_id where in_period(field.invoice_date) and field.credit_memo_count > 0) / count_distinct(field.invoice_id where in_period(field.invoice_date))

dso.notes: Defined in both Finance and RevOps; one formula.

collection_effectiveness_index_cei.formula: (sum(field.accounts_receivable) at period_start + sum(field.invoice_amount where in_period(field.invoice_date)) - sum(field.accounts_receivable) at period_end) / (sum(field.accounts_receivable) at period_start + sum(field.invoice_amount where in_period(field.invoice_date)) - sum(field.outstanding_amount where (field.snapshot_date - field.invoice_date) <= 30) at period_end)
collection_effectiveness_index_cei.notes: Billings stand in for credit sales. Current AR is receivables aged 30 days or less.

aging_buckets.notes: Reported per age bucket: outstanding amount on invoices whose age (days from invoice date to the period-end snapshot) falls in the bucket over the whole outstanding balance. Evaluate at period end.

bad_debt_rate.notes: Canonical definition is in finance.md; revops.md links to it. Denominator is GAAP recognised revenue (metric.revenue_gaap), not billings.

payment_method_distribution.formula: sum(field.invoice_amount where in_period(field.invoice_date)) / total(sum(field.invoice_amount where in_period(field.invoice_date) and field.payment_method is not null))
payment_method_distribution.notes: Reported per payment method: invoiced amount in the period paid by the method over invoiced amount with a known method.

deferred_revenue_balance.notes: Balance at period end: cumulative billed minus cumulative recognised. Finance's Deferred Revenue entry points here.

unbilled_revenue.notes: Evaluated per subscription row, so only subscriptions where recognition exceeds billing contribute.

renewal_notification_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.subscription_id where in_period(field.contract_end) and field.renewal_notified_on_time = true) / count_distinct(field.subscription_id where in_period(field.contract_end))
renewal_notification_rate.notes: Population is renewals in the period.

auto_renewal_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.subscription_id where in_period(field.contract_end) and field.auto_renewed = true) / count_distinct(field.subscription_id where in_period(field.contract_end))
auto_renewal_rate.notes: Population is renewals in the period.

daily_active_users_dau.notes: The calendar day ending at period_end. Qualifying activity is a core action defined per product, not a login.

dau_mau.notes: Source formula multiplies by 100; stored unscaled.

active_accounts.notes: Accounts with at least one active user in the period.

activation_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where in_period(field.onboarding_completion_date) and field.activation_date is not null) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where in_period(field.onboarding_completion_date))
activation_rate.notes: Onboarding-to-Active Rate: customers who completed onboarding in the period and reached activation.

feature_adoption.formula: count_distinct(field.user_id where field.feature_id is not null) / count_distinct(field.user_id where field.product_event_type = 'qualifying')
feature_adoption.notes: Evaluated per feature_id. Numerator counts users who used the feature in the period.

core_feature_adoption.formula: count_distinct(field.user_id where field.core_features_adopted = true) / count_distinct(field.user_id where field.product_event_type = 'qualifying')
core_feature_adoption.notes: Core set is 3 to 5 features defined per product. core_features_used is true when a user used all of them.

feature_depth.notes: Average feature actions per user per period.

time_to_feature_adoption.notes: Median days from a user's signup to their first use of the tracked feature, for users whose first use falls in the period. Both dates are on the user dataset (first_use_date is the first use of the feature).

breadth_of_adoption.notes: Distinct (account, feature) pairs used in the period over active accounts: the average number of features each active account uses. Both fields are on product_event.

session_duration.notes: Equivalent to total session time divided by total sessions. Unit of the session_duration field assumed minutes.

time_in_product.notes: Total session time per user per period.

pqas.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.criteria_met = true) at period_end
pqas.notes: Threshold criteria are product-specific (usage count, features activated, users added, limits reached); criteria_met is true when an account meets them.

user_retention_day_n.formula: all_time(count_distinct(field.user_id where field.product_event_type = 'qualifying' and in_period(field.signup_date) and (field.event_date - field.signup_date) = 30)) / count_distinct(field.user_id where in_period(field.signup_date))
user_retention_day_n.notes: Day 30 retention: users who signed up in the period and were active exactly 30 days after signup, over users who signed up in the period. The numerator reads all time because day 30 can fall after period_end. Change 30 for other N.

cohort_retention.formula: all_time(count_distinct(field.user_id where field.product_event_type = 'qualifying' and in_period(field.signup_date) and (field.event_date - field.signup_date) >= 49 and (field.event_date - field.signup_date) < 56)) / count_distinct(field.user_id where in_period(field.signup_date))
cohort_retention.notes: Week 8 retention for the signup cohort of the period: users who signed up in the period and had qualifying activity 49 to 55 days after signup, over users who signed up in the period. The numerator reads all time because week 8 falls after period_end.

resurrection_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.user_id where field.product_event_type = 'reactivation') / count_distinct(field.user_id where field.user_status = 'dormant') at period_start

release_frequency.notes: Releases per period, at feature or product level (distinct from code deployments).

feature_delivery_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.feature_id where in_period(field.planned_date) and field.actual_date <= field.planned_date) / count_distinct(field.feature_id where in_period(field.planned_date))

time_to_market.notes: Median days from concept approval to production release.

error_rate_user_facing.formula: count(field.event_id where field.product_event_type = 'error') / count(field.event_id where field.product_event_type in ('action', 'error'))
error_rate_user_facing.notes: Error events divided by total user actions (errors included in the denominator).

bug_escape_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.issue_id where field.issue_type = 'bug' and field.issue_environment = 'production') / count_distinct(field.issue_id where field.issue_type = 'bug')
bug_escape_rate.notes: Production bugs divided by production bugs plus bugs caught in QA. stage is 'production' or 'qa'.

uptime.notes: Total time is period_days * 1440 minutes. Scheduled maintenance counts as downtime (engineering.md).

sla_adherence.notes: Periods meeting SLA divided by total periods.

error_rate.notes: Server errors (5xx) divided by total requests.

latency_response_time.notes: Canonical value is P95. Variants p50 and p99 give the other percentiles engineering.md lists. Report percentiles rather than averages, which hide tail latency.

incident_count.notes: by_severity returns one row per severity (sev1 to sev4), because a month of sev4 noise and a month with one sev1 outage call for different responses. by_incident_type splits availability, performance, security and data incidents, which have different owners.

mean_time_to_detect_mttd.notes: Detection time minus incident start time.

mttr.notes: Resolution time minus incident start time, in minutes. by_severity returns one row per severity because resolution targets are set per severity and a blended mean hides a slow sev1. by_incident_type separates incidents whose resolution paths differ, such as a security incident and a performance regression.

change_failure_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.deployment_id where field.incident_id is not null) / count_distinct(field.deployment_id)

lead_time_for_changes.notes: Median of deploy time minus commit time.

mean_time_to_recovery_mttr.notes: recovery_time is minutes from failure to service restored per incident (ontology field), so the formula averages it directly. Mean Time to Resolve (mttr) is a separate metric that reads started_at and resolved_at.

infrastructure_utilization.notes: Measured per resource (CPU, memory, storage, network). Actual usage divided by provisioned capacity.

infrastructure_cost_per_customer.formula: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'infrastructure') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_end

headroom.notes: (Max capacity minus current usage) divided by max capacity.

vulnerability_count.notes: Categorised by severity (critical, high, medium, low).

time_to_patch.notes: Patch deploy time minus disclosure time.

revenue_gaap.notes: Recognised revenue per ASC 606, not bookings or billings.

bookings.notes: Contracted value signed in the period, from contract events. Amendments count as expansion bookings when positive.

billings.notes: by_payment_status returns one row per payment status as of period end, so finance sees how much of the period's billing is paid, unpaid, partly paid or written off.

burn_rate.notes: Net cash burn per month: cash delta over the period divided by months in the period.

magic_number.formula: (metric.arr - lag(metric.arr, 1 quarter)) / lag(window(sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm'), 1 quarter), 1 quarter)
magic_number.notes: ARR growth over the quarter ending at period_end, divided by sales and marketing spend in the quarter before that. The window makes the denominator one quarter of spend whatever the reporting period.

burn_multiple.notes: Net burn over net new ARR for the same one-month period. Net new ARR is net new MRR x 12.

opex_ratio.notes: Operating expenses are all costs outside COGS (cost_function infrastructure). by_cost_centre slices operating expenses by cost centre; the denominator stays the whole population of revenue, so the rows sum to the ratio.

collection_rate.formula: sum(field.invoice_amount where in_period(field.invoice_date) and field.payment_date is not null) / metric.billings
collection_rate.notes: Invoice-level cash: an invoice issued in the period counts at its full amount once it has a payment date. The ontology has no payment amount field, so partial payments are not measured separately.

ttfv.notes: Days from contract start to the first value milestone.

onboarding_duration.notes: Days from onboarding start to onboarding complete.

onboarding_completion.notes: Onboardings completed in the period over onboardings started in the period.

on_time_completion_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.onboarding_id where in_period(field.onboarding_completion_date) and field.onboarding_completion_date <= field.target_date) / count_distinct(field.onboarding_id where in_period(field.onboarding_completion_date))

onboarding_engagement_score.notComputable: Weighted average of engagement indicators (attendance, responsiveness, task completion, logins) whose weights the markdown does not define.

session_attendance_rate.notes: A session counts as attended when at least one attendee is recorded.

onboarding_csat.formula: count(field.satisfaction_score where field.survey_type = 'onboarding' and field.satisfaction_score >= 4) / count(field.satisfaction_score where field.survey_type = 'onboarding')
onboarding_csat.notes: Surveyed at onboarding completion. Positive means 4 or 5 on a 5 point scale.

onboarding_nps.formula: (count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'onboarding' and field.nps_score >= 9) - count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'onboarding' and field.nps_score <= 6)) / count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'onboarding') * 100
onboarding_nps.notes: Reported as a score from -100 to 100, so the x 100 is part of the definition.

implementation_quality_score.notComputable: Assessment built from qualitative components (configuration accuracy, data quality, integration health, user setup) with no stated formula or weights.

day_30_retention_post_onboarding.formula: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.onboarding_completion_date is not null and field.customer_status = 'active' and (field.last_active_date - field.onboarding_completion_date) >= 30) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.onboarding_completion_date is not null)

onboarding_cohort_churn.notComputable: A segmentation analysis of churn by onboarding duration, completeness and engagement, not a single formula.

feature_adoption_at_go_live.notes: Evaluated as a snapshot at the go-live milestone.

total_headcount.notes: Includes full-time and part-time employees. Contractors are tracked separately. by_department returns the active headcount of each department at period end.

headcount_growth_rate.formula: (metric.total_headcount at period_end - metric.total_headcount at period_start) / metric.total_headcount at period_start

employee_turnover.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.termination_date >= period_start and field.termination_date <= period_end) / ((metric.total_headcount at period_start + metric.total_headcount at period_end) / 2)
employee_turnover.notes: Calculate monthly or annually. Annualize for comparability. Average headcount is the mean of start and end headcount. by_department returns one row per department: leavers and both headcounts are counted within the department, so attrition concentrated in one team shows.

voluntary_turnover_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.termination_type = 'voluntary' and in_period(field.termination_date)) / ((metric.total_headcount at period_start + metric.total_headcount at period_end) / 2)
voluntary_turnover_rate.notes: by_department returns one row per department, the slice that points at a team or a manager when resignations cluster.

involuntary_turnover_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.termination_type = 'involuntary' and in_period(field.termination_date)) / ((metric.total_headcount at period_start + metric.total_headcount at period_end) / 2)

regrettable_turnover.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.termination_type = 'voluntary' and field.is_high_performer = true and in_period(field.termination_date)) / count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.is_high_performer = true and field.employee_status = 'active') at period_start
regrettable_turnover.notes: Denominator is high performers at period start.

average_tenure.notes: Markdown allows months or years. Months is canonical.

day_90_turnover.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.termination_date is not null and field.termination_date - field.hire_date <= 90) / count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.hire_date >= period_start and field.hire_date <= period_end)
day_90_turnover.notes: Cohort is new hires in the period. 90 days approximated as 3 months of tenure. by_hire_source returns one row per hiring source, which shows the channels that bring hires who leave inside 90 days.

enps.formula: (count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'employee' and field.nps_score >= 9) - count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'employee' and field.nps_score <= 6)) / count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'employee') * 100
enps.notes: Reported as a score from -100 to 100. Survey question: how likely are you to recommend the company as a place to work (0-10).

engagement_score.notes: Composite engagement survey score. The markdown names no formula beyond the composite, so the average of survey scores is encoded.

survey_participation_rate.formula: count(field.response_id where field.survey_type = 'employee' and field.survey_completed = true) / count(field.response_id where field.survey_type = 'employee')

time_to_fill.notes: Days from job posted to offer accepted, per filled requisition.

time_to_hire.notes: Days from candidate application to offer accepted, per hire.

offer_acceptance_rate.formula: count(field.requisition_id where field.offer_status = 'accepted') / count(field.requisition_id where field.offer_status in ('accepted', 'declined'))

quality_of_hire.formula: avg(field.performance_rating where field.hire_date is not null and field.snapshot_date - field.hire_date >= 182 and field.snapshot_date - field.hire_date <= 365)
quality_of_hire.notes: Average performance rating of hires at 6-12 months. The markdown also allows the share of hires meeting or exceeding expectations, which needs a rating threshold it does not define.

cost_per_hire.formula: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'recruiting') / count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.hire_date >= period_start and field.hire_date <= period_end)

source_of_hire.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where in_period(field.hire_date)) / total(count_distinct(field.employee_id where in_period(field.hire_date)))
source_of_hire.notes: Reported per hire source: hires in the period through the source over all hires in the period, read on the period-end employee snapshot.

pay_equity_ratio.formula: avg(field.salary where field.underrepresented_group = true) / avg(field.salary where field.underrepresented_group = false)
pay_equity_ratio.notes: Compare within the same role. Group A and group B are encoded as underrepresented and other groups. Target 0.98-1.02.

diversity_representation.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.underrepresented_group = true and field.employee_status = 'active') / count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.employee_status = 'active') at period_end
diversity_representation.notes: Track overall and by department or level.

diversity_in_leadership.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.underrepresented_group = true and field.job_level in ('manager', 'director', 'vp', 'c_level') and field.employee_status = 'active') / count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.job_level in ('manager', 'director', 'vp', 'c_level') and field.employee_status = 'active') at period_end

diversity_hiring_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.underrepresented_group = true and field.hire_date >= period_start and field.hire_date <= period_end) / count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.hire_date >= period_start and field.hire_date <= period_end)

visitors.notes: Sum of per-source unique visitors: web_traffic is keyed by traffic_source, so a visitor arriving through two sources counts once in each. Load one row per source per reporting period so a returning visitor is not counted again within a source.

leads.notes: New leads captured in the period. by_lead_source returns one row per lead source. by_lead_stage returns one row per stage at period end of the period's new leads, which shows how far the intake has progressed.

mqls.notes: by_lead_source returns one row per lead source, the slice marketing budgets are set against.

lead_to_mql_rate.notes: by_lead_source returns one row per lead source with both counts taken within the source, so a source that brings volume but little qualified interest shows.

mql_to_sql_rate.notes: by_lead_source returns one row per lead source, which shows where sales rejects marketing's leads.

lvr.notes: Uses qualified leads (MQLs), not raw leads.

marketing_cac.formula: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm' and field.cost_centre = 'marketing') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'new')

cac_by_channel.formula: sum(field.ad_spend) / count_distinct(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))
cac_by_channel.notes: Reported per marketing channel. Spend is campaign ad spend, which carries its channel, rather than the cost ledger: cost_event rows have a cost function but no channel, so ledger cost cannot be split by channel. New customers are opportunities won in the period, attributed to their first-touch channel.

cpl.formula: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm' and field.cost_centre = 'marketing') / metric.leads

cost_per_mql.formula: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm' and field.cost_centre = 'marketing') / metric.mqls

marketing_sourced_pipeline.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.marketing_source = 'marketing' and field.opportunity_stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost'))

marketing_sourced_revenue.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.marketing_source = 'marketing' and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))
marketing_sourced_revenue.notes: First-touch attribution on closed won revenue.

marketing_influenced_pipelinerevenue.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.marketing_influenced = true and field.opportunity_stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost'))

variants.revenue: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.marketing_influenced = true and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

marketing_influenced_pipelinerevenue.notes: Multi-touch attribution: any marketing touch. Main formula is pipeline, the revenue variant covers closed won.

paid_media_efficiency_roas.formula: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.channel = 'paid_ads' and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / sum(field.ad_spend where field.channel = 'paid_ads')
paid_media_efficiency_roas.notes: Expressed as a ratio such as 3x.

email_metrics.notComputable: A family of six email rates (open, click, click-to-open, unsubscribe, bounce, spam complaint) with no single headline metric. The ontology has no email send dataset or fields for sends, deliveries, opens, clicks, unsubscribes, bounces or complaints, so none of the six is encoded.

content_performance.notComputable: A family of content measures (downloads, engagement rate, content-to-MQL) with no single metric.

brand_awareness.notComputable: Survey-based or search volume proxy with no defined formula.

nps_marketing_context.formula: (count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'prospect' and field.nps_score >= 9) - count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'prospect' and field.nps_score <= 6)) / count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'prospect') * 100
nps_marketing_context.notes: Same NPS arithmetic applied to prospect and market respondents rather than customers.

onboarding_milestone_completion_rate.formula: all_time(count(field.onboarding_id where in_period(field.milestone_due_date) and field.milestone_date is not null and field.milestone_date <= period_end)) / all_time(count(field.onboarding_id where in_period(field.milestone_due_date)))
onboarding_milestone_completion_rate.notes: Milestones reached over milestones due: onboarding milestones due in the period that were reached by period end, over all milestones due in the period. Each row of onboarding_milestone is one planned milestone, so planned rows carry milestone_due_date before milestone_date is set; all_time keeps unreached rows that the milestone_date period filter would drop. Add field.onboarding_milestone = '<milestone>' to both sides for a single milestone.

professional_services_milestone_completi.formula: count_distinct(field.project_milestone_id where in_period(field.actual_date) and field.actual_date <= field.planned_date) / count_distinct(field.project_milestone_id where in_period(field.actual_date))
professional_services_milestone_completi.notes: Milestones delivered in the period that met their planned date.

product_activation_rate.formula: count_distinct(field.user_id where in_period(field.signup_date) and field.activation_date is not null) / count_distinct(field.user_id where in_period(field.signup_date))
product_activation_rate.notes: Users who signed up in the period and reached the activation milestone. The milestone is product-specific and must be defined explicitly.
